questions.prompt: What core principle of gravity does Keating attribute to Galileo against Aristotle?
choices: A Heavier objects always fall faster.
B All masses fall at the same rate.
C Only metals fall; wood floats in vacuum.
D Gravity works only on Earth.
questions.explain: Galileo's insight: all masses fall alike (absent air resistance complications).

questions.prompt: Keating says Newton's gravitational force law has which mathematical behavior (on relevant scales)?
choices: C Linear growth with distance forever.
questions.explain: He highlights the inverse-square relation of Newtonian gravity.

questions.prompt: According to Keating, where does the word "galaxy" come from?
choices: B Greek terms related to milky circles.
questions.explain: He ties galaxy to Greek galactikos kuklos / milky circles.

questions.prompt: William Herschel's early Milky Way map, Keating notes, placed us where?
choices: B At the center of the galaxy.
D At the Galactic North Pole only.
questions.explain: Herschel's crude map put us at the galactic center—a cosmic ego theme.

questions.prompt: The 1920 "Great Debate" Keating recounts featured which two astronomers?
choices: B Harlow Shapley and Heber Curtis.
questions.explain: Shapley vs Curtis debated the nature/extent of the Milky Way and nebulae.
